sectorSummary.overview: Domestic demand, new products and richer vehicle content support strong growth across the ten available calls. Profit conversion varies as commodity inflation, wage increases and new-capacity costs weigh on some companies; SJS lowers its relative growth outlook even as it raises margin guidance. Several longer-term opportunities still depend on commissioning and customer ramp-up.

trends.text: New products, customer programs and greater content per vehicle support growth beyond existing volumes.
Capacity expansion and new facilities support growth plans but require investment and successful ramp-up.

tailwinds.text: Healthy domestic automotive demand and premiumization support the current order and revenue environment.

headwinds.text: Inflation in materials, freight, currencies or wages raises costs or complicates customer price recovery.

opportunities.text: Seating and adjacent vehicle systems open new markets through partnerships, with future scale dependent on customer wins.
ADS, export programs and electrification diversify growth beyond traditional auto components.

risks.text: Endurance shifts ABS program starts; near-term growth plans remain sensitive to commissioning and customer execution.
SJS reduces its FY27 relative growth outlook as consumer demand and product rationalization weigh on revenue.
Sansera’s higher capex and working capital increase net debt, while Gabriel adds financing for strategic expansion.

insights.text: ASK’s reported revenue growth includes alloy-price pass-through; its management-adjusted net growth provides a separate view.
Order-book measures differ: Sansera separates five-year ADS lifetime orders from non-ADS peak annual sales, and NDR’s DYA opportunity extends to FY31.
